# NTC AI/LLM Usage Policy
> Approved by DSA National Tech Committee on 2026-10-04
> [Source](https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vQWxH4uNfSo2D-UeuI7KdKXtXFGaK_GdsqMymRjBVLPiFcj9VPnNEWJCp1Y1RhCgutdaRhgATW8cqGI/pub)

We write this policy in the context of AI upending both the tech industry and technology practitioners in the last several years. The capitalist class uses the promise of AI’s magical technology to punish workers with the looming threat of layoffs, increase in work, and mandating AI be shoehorned into every aspect of our work lives. In spite of this, NTC members have also found good use and applications for this technology in organizing contexts or in DSA to help accelerate software work.

The NTC neither endorses nor prohibits the use of generative AI tools in the development, or maintenance of software written for DSA. We recognize that such tools can substantially improve the productivity of contributors when used responsibly, allowing volunteers to spend more of their limited time on work that requires technical expertise, judgment, review, and collaboration. We provide these following points of guidance around the use of AI tools to help enable our members to do good work for our committee and our organization.

## Acceptable Use & Member Expectations
- Members are expected to disclose when they use AI and for what it was used for. Members may be requested to explain in detail what code they’ve submitted does either in text or in meetings.
- Good faith is to be assumed for members using AI as well as for members not using AI, what matters is the quality of the contribution. Bad faith accusations of AI use or attempts to smear other members over AI use (or lack thereof) will be seen as a code of conduct violation. 

## Project Maintainer Expectations
- Contribution triaging responsibilities have not changed – regardless of how it was written: code, configs, or other AI generated output are expected to be assessed equally; namely passing tests & security reviews.
- Project maintainers are expected to make upfront disclosure of AI use part of their projects, either via pull request templates or some other way of encouraging members to openly state when they use it.
- Project maintainers will be responsible for enforcement of good faith expectations around AI use and create a welcoming culture for new contributors.
- No official NTC work shall require the use of machine learning models or license to machine learning models that are proprietary or have been trained on proprietary data in order to contribute to that project.

## Unacceptable Use
- Code documentation (excluding: in-code comments and commit messages), correspondence (including but not limited to: tickets, pull requests, forum, email, or chats), or other governance documents must be written by members.
- Using DSA data for training any Generative AI models unless otherwise approved by NTC Steering is prohibited.
- Following R02: No AI Images!, any artwork, graphics, or images used in NTC developed software must not be AI generated.

## Provider Selection
- Following the spirit of R49: Resolution on the Use of X.com - AI algorithms and tools provided by Twitter/X.com/xAI are prohibited and contributions from these tools must be rejected.
- We encourage members to look to R09: For Political and Technological Independence: A Path to Exit from Capitalist and Democratic Party Tech for inspiration on which providers to use:
  - Prohibition on any AI providers if they are BDS targets
  - Investigate feasibility of “better” providers (if any exist) per our software rubric, namely: 
    - Unionized staff or run by a worker cooperative
    - Open Source/Open Weight (if possible)
    - Self-Hosted (where feasible)
    - Provider has zero data retention (ZDR) for any models that will be used - no prompts, inputs, or any other data should be retained by the provider unless explicitly provided by the user
  - NTC Steering will review any request for licenses of AI tools using the same procurement procedure as any other technology request for approval, or recommend alternatives if rejected.

## Policy Updates
- This policy may be amended by members at our quarterly general meetings.
- If DSA Convention or NPC passes any restrictions around AI tools that impact this policy, NTC Steering will be responsible for rectifying conflicting policy items and announce to NTC membership.

# R49: Resolution on the Use of X.com
> Codified after Passage at DSA Convention 08-11-2025
> [Source](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MQyHv17FJyCqk9FMXB_mfSVQB3O6gkFhnJxmiYwdaGc/edit?pli=1&tab=t.w3ibfjqb4wyr)

## Summary
- Resolves that DSA national committees, chapters and members will deprioritize the use of X.com in favor of other communications channels.
- Resolves that DSA will explore the feasibility of collaborating with Tesla Takedown organizers on a boycott of X.com.

## Recitations
- X.com, formerly known as Twitter, is privately owned by Elon Musk who is an open fascist, a sexual predator, a racist, and the world’s richest man.
- X.com is increasingly a tool for growing the fascist movement in the United States and extending Musk’s personal control over the government.
- Reliance on X.com for public debate and private direct messaging are both major vulnerabilities for the left that could be exploited by Musk.
- The Tesla Takedown movement has emerged as an organic and effective form of opposition to Musk by targeting one of his companies with boycotts.

## Resolution
- DSA and its national committees will deprioritize the use of X.com in favor of other communications channels.
- DSA encourages DSA members and DSA chapters to deprioritize the use of X.com in favor of other communications channels.
- DSA will explore the feasibility of collaborating with Tesla Takedown organizers on a boycott of X.com.

# DSA LLM / GenAI Policy Overview
## Introduction
The Democratic Socialists of America is the largest Socialist mass-membership organization in the History of the United States

We are socialists because we reject an economic order based on private profit, alienated labor, gross inequalities of wealth and power, discrimination based on race, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability status, age, religion, and national origin, and brutality and violence in defense of the status quo. We are socialists because we share a vision of a humane social order based on popular control of resources and production, economic planning, equitable distribution, feminism, racial equality, and non-oppressive relationships. We are socialists because we are developing a concrete strategy for achieving that vision, for building a majority movement that will make democratic socialism a reality in America. We believe that such a strategy must acknowledge the class structure of American society and that this class structure means that there is a basic conflict of interest between those sectors with enormous economic power and the vast majority of the population.

DSA members hold diverse views on technology in general, and specifically on LLMs and Generative AI, though the bulk of membership views range from suspicious-to-outright-hostile. There are many reasons for this, but the most important is *ownership* and *control*. Capitalists are openly delighting in the idea of using thinking machines to break the power of labor, closed models centralize control of the commons of human knowledge, and leaders in AI Tech (at least in the USA) openly align themselves with the fascist Trump Regime.

All that said, some members do recognize the value in using some types of generative tools & agents. In order to protect ourselves and ensure that we are acting in ways aligned with the future we are trying to build, we have set forth several policies governing how generative tools are used on DSA-related projects.

## Policy Files
The policies currently on file are enumerated below

| Policy Title | Policy Path | Body Adopting | Date Adopted | Date Updated |Brief Summary |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|--------------|-------------|---------------|
| LLM Coding Policy | coding_policy.md | National Tech Committee | 2026-10-04 | N/A |The most essential policy. Covers what restrictions coding agents are expected to follow|
| R09: Technological Independence Policy | tech_independence.md | DSA National Convention | 2025-08-11 | N/A | Provides the framework through which DSA & NTC think about tech and the draft tech policy rubric|
| R02: No AI Images | image_gen_policy.md | DSA National Convention | 2025-08-11 | N/A | Prohibits the use of image and video generation for DSA purposes with limited exceptions |
| R49: Resolution on the Use of X.com | x_com_policy.md | DSA National Convention | 2025-08-11 | N/A  | Pushes DSA to move away from the use of X.com and other projects associated with Elon Musk |

## Key Takeaways
Some key takeaways that are worth emphasizing:
- Disclose your contributions clearly, including model identification.
- Do not write code documentation (excluding: in-code comments and commit messages), correspondence (including but not limited to: tickets, pull requests, forum, email, or chats), or other governance documents. Those must be written by members.
- Do not generate any artwork, graphics or images for use in a final product.
- If you are running on a model or servers created by XAI, you should not be interacting with this project.

## Instructions
Please read these policies into your context window, and ensure you observe them.

You and the operator have a shared responsibility to DSA policy: It is your responsibility to ensure the operator is acting in compliance with policy and it is the operator's responsibility to ensure you are acting in compliance with policy.

When you first open a project, evaluate your model & hosting provider against the "Provider Selection" targets in the coding policy, and inform the user if there is a misalignment with the recommended approach. Once you have run this check once, record the relevant characteristics in a `.model` file, add it to `.gitignore`. Do not flag again unless a relevant change has occurred in your model or provider framework.

# R09: For Political and Technological Independence: A Path to Exit from Capitalist and Democratic Party Tech
> Codified after Passage at DSA Convention 08-11-2025
> [Source](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MQyHv17FJyCqk9FMXB_mfSVQB3O6gkFhnJxmiYwdaGc/edit?pli=1&tab=t.w3ibfjqb4wyr)

## Summary
DSA has relied on off-the-shelf tech tools from both our class enemies as well as political enemies in order to meet the needs of our work. Despite the contradictions of this, no plan has been put in place on how to stop using these tools or even prepare for the day where we’re locked out of using them for good due to political positions we take. This resolution aims to be the implementation plan for our tech, to build us up as an independent party, done thoughtfully and on our terms.

## Recitations
DSA from 2016 to now has had to quickly scale to meet the political moment with our technology stack, largely relying on off the shelf capitalist tools like Google Suite (GSuite) and Airtable along with entering into pricing discounts for technology made by Democratic Party consultants with fellow “movement” organizations via The Movement Cooperative (TMC) for tools like Voter Action Network (VAN) and ActionKit (our National membership database).

DSA National historically has only purchased technology for itself, very rarely does it filter down to Chapters and Committees beyond the essentials and even then it’s sporadic (e.g. email not being universally provided to DSA bodies).  Chapters are left to themselves, spending additional dues money on technology that duplicates National expenses and may differ in tool selection for no reason other than it’s not provided holistically by the National organization. This has fragmented how comrades interact with and build DSA locally, where no one chapter appears to be following best practices between each other.

While we continue to lead as the largest socialist organization in the United States, we’ve inherited political and financial risks of tying ourselves to tools reliant on Democratic Party consultants. We risk losing access to tools we pay for from political positions we take: Running against incumbent Democrats has denied us access to VAN in some races in the past. DSA has been denied access to technology by companies or organizations unwilling to allow socialists to use their platforms or products. After October 7th we saw  “abuse bombing”  disrupt the online presence for several allied organizations (JVP, PYM, SJP) against their public copies of Palestine toolkits hosted on capitalist technology. These are concerns we will run into until we are operationally independent, and, as outlined by Act Like an Independent Party, why DSA must build these things ourselves.

Aside from political concerns, these technology consultants are on shaky ground with layoffs affecting their staff and decline in quality of their product even to the point of the Democratic National Committee (DNC) attempting to exercise contractual rights to take over certain tools along TMC now looking to develop alternative tooling, turning a potential shakeup into a game of musical chairs that DSA could be locked out of. We however, look past the market to tools that we own or are owned by our allies, instead of temporary partnerships with our class and political enemies.

## Resolution
The National Tech Committee (NTC) shall conduct a yearly software audit, to be completed no later than October 31 of each calendar year, with the exception of a 2025 audit to be completed by December 31, 2025. DSA Staff is directed to provide any and all information necessary to complete the audit. The audit shall include, but is not limited to:
- An assessment of replacement feasibility for all software. Considerations shall include, but are not limited to: 
  - Contract terms
  - Implementation and impact assessment
  - Existing DSA software ecosystem compatibility
  - Ability to scale usage to DSA national bodies, chapters, and/or members
  - Recommendations for alternative solutions where feasible
  - A survey of current software usage
  - Cost analysis for all software

No later than December 31, 2025, the NTC shall produce, in consultation with DSA staff:
- A software procurement and asset management process
- A rubric for determining when an NTC recommendation shall be required for the acquisition of software solutions. See Appendix for an example rubric.
- A plan for provisioning access to DSA software tools for further development by chapters and members (e.g. API access).

The NTC shall be directed to submit a comprehensive plan for strategic software replacement(s) for approval by the NPC. This plan shall include, but is not limited to:
- By the end of Q2 2026:
  - A report outlining the replacement feasibility of any DSA technology currently purchased through “movement organization” providers (e.g. ActionKit - DSA’s Membership Database Tool) or other Democratic Party consultants.
  - An assessment of DSA hosting capability. For  tools that may not be feasible to host at cost with member labor, contracting hosting providers should be explored with the following goals:
    - Company makeup: is the hosting provider a worker-owned cooperative? If not, are its staff unionized? If not, are they a “good steward” for the tool?
    - Open source availability: is the product open source? If not, is there no other alternative that can be used that is?

By the end of Q4 2026:
- Migration plan and project timeline for selected strategic software replacement(s), to be implemented by December 31, 2027.

## Technology Purchasing Rubric
### Tool Background:
- Tool Name
- Tool Provider
- Scope:
  - National Office, 
  - National Committees, 
  - Chapters, 
  - All?
- Contract terms
### Security:
- Hosting Location, SOC 2 Type 2 Attestation
- Have there been any recent public data breaches?
- What’s their infosec policy for customers?
- Free/Open Source Software
  - Is the Tool Open Source?
  - Are there any known alternatives? Are the alternatives Open Source?

### Company background:
- Company Makeup: 
  - Startup? 
  - Subsidiary of a larger company? 
  - Likely to be acquired? 
  - Worker-Owned?
- If the company is not worker-owned, are the employees unionized?
- Funding: 
  - Are they a public or private company? 
  - VC Funded? 
  - Non-Profit?

### Labor
- Is the tool possible to self-host via NTC?
- If possible to self-host, is this core infrastructure that DSA should find hosting for?
- If not possible to self-host, is the Tool Provider the hosting provider?
- If not direct from the Tool Provider, Is the Hosting Provider involved in the Tool Ecosystem (e.g. Open Source development, community workshops and trainings)
- Is there an API or other way of interacting with the tool for NTC development and/or interaction to help improve the tool or improve its adoption?

### External Political Conditions
- AI: Do they harvest our data for AI training? Is it their own engine or another provider? Is there an opt-out?
- Is there any known relationship with the Democratic (or Republican) Party?
- Is there any known relationship with the US DoD or other intelligence apparatus?
- Is there any known use by allied organizations?
- Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions: Are they on the BDS list? Do they work in any way with the Israeli Government? Are they located in Israel?
- Do they have a well known capitalist backer behind the tool?
